_readme: Script `voice:` key  ->  casting role id (progress_media/casting/CASTING.html).
The scripts address speakers by their own keys; casting is organised per role.
Without this map nothing resolves, and EclipseGenerateVoicesCommandlet skips a
voice asset with an empty ElevenLabsVoiceId at Display level -- so unmapped
lines are never generated AND never reported as missing.
Enforced by Eclipse/Tools/check_voice_resolves.py (runs in verify.ps1).
Adding a speaker to a script means adding it here in the same commit.
`slot` picks which voice inside a multi-voice role (bark registers A/B/C/D).
`variants` means one script key ships in several cast voices -- Voss is written
once and voiced per player gender, so those lines cost double.
RULING L1-R30: `eclipse_fighter_c` and `_d` are RETIRED, not aliased. Their
eight lines were all Iron Chorus and now carry `iron_chorus_fighter_a` / `_b`.
They are not re-added as aliases, and that is the point: an alias is two keys
on one ROLE (dex / dex_callum are one man), but these are two keys on one
role+SLOT -- and the collision check groups by `role:slot`, so it would never
see two factions sharing one voice. A silent share is the exact defect this
file exists to prevent.

iron_chorus_fighter_a.note: The rival cell's two people, not Ember's (RULING L1-R30). The ROLE stays `eclipse_fighter` on purpose while O-16 is open: the owner's proposal offers slot C (Beth) and slot D (Arric) under that role id, and resolve_casting_choice.py derives slots_needed from THIS file. Retargeting the role now would leave the owner's button pointing at nothing. Splitting the role is the second half of L1-R30 and it is an owner file.

_readme: Speakers the scripts use that have NO role in 19_voice_production.md §19.3.
They are not a mapping problem -- they are a casting-table gap. Listed here so
the checker can report them as 'known and undecided' instead of failing every
run, but they still cannot be generated until the owner casts them.
